item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 120531
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located near the coast of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP93):
A broad area of low pressure has formed several hundred miles south
of the coast of Guatemala, accompanied by some shower and
thunderstorm activity. This system has become better defined since
yesterday, and environmental conditions are forecast to be
conducive for further development. A tropical depression is
expected to form well south of southern Mexico in a few days while
the system moves generally west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Blake

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 120853
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
...SIMON DRIFTING NORTHWEST...
...DANGEROUS WINDS AND FLOODING RAINS CONTINUE ALONG
THE COAST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.0N 106.3W
ABOUT 145 MI...235 KM WNW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 50 MI...75 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...115 MPH...185 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...958 MB...28.29 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Playa Perula to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* North of El Roblito to Bahia Tempehuaya
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area within 48 hours.

Interests elsewhere in west-central Mexico should continue to 
monitor as changes to watches and warnings are possible later today.

For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 20.0 North, longitude 106.3 West. Simon is moving 
toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this general motion 
is expected to continue into early Tuesday. A gradual turn toward 
the northeast is forecast thereafter, and Simon is expected to move 
inland across west-central Mexico around midweek.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 115 mph (185 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Simon is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Slow weakening is forecast to continue, 
however Simon is expected to remain a hurricane through midweek. 
Rapid weakening is likely after Simon moves inland.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles
(95 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 958 mb (28.29 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are likely occuring in the Hurricane
Warning area, with hurricane conditions spreading northward today 
into Monday. Hurricane conditions are possible within the
watch area by Wednesday, with tropical storm conditions possible by
Tuesday night.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of 
2 to 4 inches across coastal portions of southwest and west-central 
Mexico with isolated additional amounts of 6 to 8 inches over 
portions of the state of Jalisco into the early portion of the week 
and the state of Sinaloa mainly Wednesday and Thursday.  Isolated 
maximum storm totals of 30 inches are possible over portions of the 
states of Michoacan, Colima, and Jalisco.  This rainfall will 
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides or worsen any 
on-going flooding, especially in areas of steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the immediate
coast near and to the east of where the center approaches land. Near
the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and destructive
waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 500 AM MST.
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Blake

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 120251
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 PM MST Sun Oct 11 2026
 
Simon is showing signs of weakening this evening, likely due to its 
prolonged close proximity to the Mexican coastline and the 
associated negative affects of nearby mountainous terrain. Infrared 
satellite imagery indicates warming cloud tops within the convection 
in the northeastern quadrant, with mid-level dry air beginning to 
wrap around the western side of the cyclone. Recent objective Dvorak 
intensity estimates have decreased over the past several hours and 
range from 99-110 kt. Based on the deteriorating satellite 
presentation and the lower intensity estimates, the initial 
intensity is set at 105 kt for this advisory. 

The major hurricane is moving slowly north-northwestward, steered by 
a mid-level ridge centered over the south-central United States. 
Simon is forecast to track parallel to the coast of west-central 
Mexico over the next day or so. However, its continued close 
proximity to land will likely bring hurricane conditions to portions 
of the warning area, particularly near Cabo Corrientes, even though 
the core is forecast to remain just offshore. Around midweek, a 
strong upper-level low moving across the western United States is 
expected to induce a turn toward the north and then northeast. 
Although there remains some model spread, an increasing number of 
the hurricane regional models and consensus aids, including HCCA, 
bring Simon onshore around midweek. The latest NHC forecast is very 
similar to the previous advisory, showing Simon moving inland and 
dissipating in the day 3-4 period. 

Gradual weakening is expected due to the proximity to the 
mountainous terrain, which could further disrupt the hurricane's 
structure along its eastern side. A slight increase in wind shear 
and the entrainment of drier mid-level air should further contribute 
to the weakening trend. However, as Simon turns northward then 
northeastward around midweek, it is forecast to move over very warm 
waters of 31-32 C, which could limit further weakening before 
landfall. The latest NHC forecast has been nudged upward slightly 
beyond 12 h, with Simon expected to maintain hurricane strength 
through landfall. This forecast lies near the middle of the 
intensity guidance envelope. Rapid weakening is expected once Simon 
moves inland, and dissipation is forecast by 96 h. 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are 
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a 
Hurricane Warning is in effect from Playa Perula to El Roblito. 
Residents should continue to shelter in a safe room to ride out the 
storm as the most significant hazards are ongoing.

2. Simon is expected to approach the coast of western Mexico later 
this week, where hurricane conditions are possible. A Hurricane 
Watch is in effect from El Roblito to Bahia Tempehuaya. 

3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern and west-central Mexico over the next few days. This 
rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
4. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico over the next few days. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.

$$
